post.caption: A king's grave inspired Napoleon's golden bees. The tomb of King Childeric was found at Tournai in 1653, and a gold ring found inside carried the king's name. Reports say some 300 gold insects were found, and only two survive with wings inlaid with garnet. Experts still debate whether they were bees or cicadas. Napoleon wanted symbols that tied his dynasty to France's origins, and golden bees decorated his coronation on 2 December 1804. An adviser pitched the bee as a republic with a chief, because people then thought a hive's queen was a king.
